facts.text: Nominally equimolar CoCrFeNiTi powders were subjected to high-energy ball milling for 1–6 h in argon.
The milled powders were consolidated by spark plasma sintering under vacuum at 900–1000 °C for 10 min.
High-energy ball milling was performed at 400 rpm with a 20:1 ball-to-powder mass ratio.
Spark plasma sintering used a heating rate of 50 °C/min and a 30.4 mm-diameter mold.
Prolonged milling generated severe lattice strain and reduced the crystallite size to below 48 nm, promoting a nonequilibrium nanocrystalline solid solution.
Spark plasma sintering promoted rapid diffusion and densification while suppressing porosity.
After sintering at 1000 °C, the microstructure comprised approximately 83% FCC and 17% BCC phases.
The strength and hardness enhancement was attributed to the combined effects of Hall–Petch grain-boundary strengthening, milling-induced dislocation accumulation, and solid-solution strengthening.
The milled and SPS-consolidated alloy had higher hardness and compressive strength than the cast CoCrFeNiTi baseline.
At a sintering temperature of 1000 °C, the alloy reached a Vickers hardness of 675 Hv.
At a sintering temperature of 1000 °C, the alloy reached a compressive strength of 1894 MPa.
At a sintering temperature of 1000 °C, the alloy exhibited a yield stress of 1238 MPa.
